methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort of 50 head-and-neck RIM patients (2003-2024) using the Cahan/Arlen/Murray criteria — an accepted operational definition — with exclusions for incomplete follow-up and thyroid RIMs. Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank tests is appropriate for the primary survival comparison. However, no multivariable adjustment (Cox regression) is performed despite substantial baseline imbalance between surgical and non-surgical groups (driven largely by resectability/comorbidity), which creates confounding by indication that the authors discuss only qualitatively. Dosimetric and chemotherapy details are incomplete. The authors themselves note that non-radical surgery results should be interpreted with caution due to small R2 subgroup (n=1). No sample size or power calculation given.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: RIMs are rare and underreported; the paper reinforces radical surgery as the treatment of choice and documents long latency and site/histology patterns relevant for long-term survivorship programs. Findings are clinically actionable for counseling and surveillance of HNC survivors, especially those treated at <45 years. Classified Oxford LoE 4 as a single-center retrospective case series with no comparison cohort of de novo tumors or contemporaneous control.

reporting_quality.justification: As a retrospective observational cohort, STROBE applies; core elements (inclusion criteria, setting, variable definitions, outcome, survival analysis) are present, and the authors explicitly disclose missingness in dosimetric and chemotherapy data. However, no STROBE checklist is invoked, there is no flow diagram (only text mention of 10 exclusions), and baseline characteristics between subgroups are described narratively rather than in a full comparison table. No data or code availability statement is present; individual-level data are not shared. Institutional ethics approval number and consent waiver status are not explicit in the extracted text.

novelty_literature.justification: The work is a descriptive single-center series on a well-studied entity; most findings (surgery confers survival benefit, R0 margins matter, nasopharynx as primary site common, latency ~20 years) replicate prior reports (Liu et al., Tay et al., Chung et al., Sale et al.). Novel observations are limited to modest descriptive findings (heterogeneous histology in smokers, longer latency for age <=45). No molecular or dosimetric mechanistic advance. Incremental confirmation of known findings.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear Methods, Results, and Discussion, and survival curves, two representative clinical vignettes, and a thoughtful limitations paragraph aid interpretation. Minor issues include a handful of typos ('candided', 'Linical', 'PMC' numbers run-on), formatting glitches in the inclusion criteria block, and a reporting inconsistency (R2 2-year OS of 100% with a single patient who died before 5 years). Overall presentation supports understanding.

key_strengths: Application of rigorous Cahan/Arlen/Murray criteria to define RIMs
Clear demonstration of survival benefit with radical surgery over systemic therapy alone (5-year OS 57.5% vs 0%)
Reasonably large single-center series (n=50) for a rare entity with 20-year accrual period
Transparent acknowledgment of dosimetric and chemotherapy data gaps and of selection bias in surgical versus non-surgical comparisons
Includes informative illustrative cases and relevant dosimetric observations (sarcomas more often in high-dose GTV regions)
key_concerns: No multivariable Cox adjustment; confounding by indication between surgery and non-surgery groups unaddressed
Incomplete radiotherapy dose/fractionation and chemotherapy data across patients
Findings are largely confirmatory of existing literature with limited novelty
No data sharing statement; STROBE checklist not invoked; no flow diagram
Statistical anomaly in R2 subgroup (n=1) reporting; small numbers limit histology subgroup inferences
Potential misclassification of some SCCs arising in irradiated smokers as RIMs rather than de novo tumors (acknowledged)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically useful but methodologically and analytically modest single-center series on a rare entity; appropriate for a tier-3 head-and-neck or general-oncology journal after major revisions to add multivariable analysis and improved reporting.
